questions.question: Name the three participants in the circular flow of a closed economy and state two roles of each.
questions.expected_answer: Households: own and supply the factors of production and receive factor incomes; consume goods and services; pay taxes; save. Businesses: produce and sell goods and services; hire factors of production and pay wages, rent, interest and profit; invest in capital goods; pay taxes. Government: collects taxes; buys goods and services; employs labour and pays salaries; provides public goods and services; pays transfer payments (grants); regulates the economy.

questions.question: Distinguish between a closed and an open economy, and state which one South Africa is.
questions.expected_answer: A closed economy has no trade with other countries (no imports, exports or cross-border flows); an open economy trades with the rest of the world and has a fourth participant, the foreign sector. South Africa is an open economy; the closed economy is a simplified model.

questions.question: Classify each payment: (a) a nurse's salary, (b) the old age grant, (c) a family buying groceries, (d) company tax paid by a factory.
questions.expected_answer: (a) Government buying labour in the factor market (household income). (b) A transfer payment from government to a household, with nothing given in return. (c) Household spending (consumption) in the goods and services market; business revenue. (d) A tax paid by a business to the government.
